newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico hydrocarbon levels above expectations - govt.
newsitem.headline: Mexico hydrocarbon levels above expectations - govt.

text.p: A review of hydrocarbon reserves in Mexico's marine production region found "more than expected," Energy Minister Jesus Reyes Heroles told reporters Wednesday, adding that results of the study will be made public in January.

"We have already done calculations for reserves in the marine region and will continue doing studies for the next three years. The results not only confirm reserve levels, but in some cases are more than expected," he said.
Reyes Heroles said no new fields had been discovered recently, but that state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) was conducting explorations and working to extend existing fields.
"The country's hydrocarbon levels are beyond safe and reasonable margins, in fact, some of the fields are under-exploited," Reyes Heroles said.
One of Pemex's projects planned for next year is to expand the Cantarell oil field, the marine region's largest field with an average production of 961,000 barrels per day (bpd) in 1994.
The marine region is Mexico's most lucrative petroleum source with output for 1994 totalling more than two million bpd.
